title: Water Recovery System UPA fault tolerance
body: Urine Processor Assembly (UPA) shall be tolerant to recycle-loop calcium buildup; if conductivity > 5000 µS/cm, halt UPA, schedule manual cleaning. ISS retains ~250 days of water reserve at any time to bridge UPA outage.
citation: ISS Water Recovery Subsystem Lessons Learned (NASA, 2017)

title: OGS hydrogen sensor
body: Oxygen Generation System (OGS) ppH2 in cabin shall not exceed 0.4 % LEL. If exceeded, shut down OGS, vent hydrogen line, switch to backup oxygen via SFOG candles or Elektron.

title: Fire response: detection, suppression, recovery
body: On smoke detector alarm: 1. Crew dons portable breathing apparatus (PBA). 2. Power down affected rack. 3. Apply CO2 portable fire extinguisher (PFE) into firepoint port. 4. Monitor combustion-product gas analyzer for re-ignition. 5. Vent module if smoke persists.

title: Cabin pressure decay
body: If cabin pressure drops > 0.7 psi/hr (4.8 kPa/hr) and not attributable to commanded depress, isolate suspected module via hatch close. Crew safe-haven posture (Soyuz/Crew Dragon). Diagnose leak via PPRV / leak-locator.

title: Ammonia / toxic atmosphere intrusion
body: If cabin ammonia > 30 ppm or any toxic-atmosphere alarm, crew dons PBA, retreats to safe-haven module, and isolates affected segment. Reverse-flow scrubbers activated; ventilation isolated until atmosphere clears.

title: CDRA bed temperature high
body: If CDRA bed temperature > 220 °C during heating cycle, suspected channel blockage. Halt cycle, switch to redundant CDRA, schedule channel-purge maintenance EVA / IVA.

title: CMG bearing temperature trending high
body: If CMG bearing temperature trends > 65 °C with stable load, schedule wheel-speed reduction during quiescent ops. Persistent > 80 °C indicates incipient failure; switch authority to remaining CMGs and schedule replacement.

title: SAA crew radiation sheltering
body: During South Atlantic Anomaly (SAA) high-flux passes, crew shall not perform EVAs. Radiation-sensitive experiments paused. ISS attitude bias may be commanded to maximise mass-shielding of crew quarters during SPE (Solar Particle Event).

title: Late-notice conjunction sheltering
body: If conjunction warning received with TCA < 12 hours and Pc > 1e-4 but PDAM not feasible, crew shall shelter in Soyuz/Crew Dragon for the close-approach window. Hatches closed. Module non-essential power down.

title: Crew sleep-cycle protection during nominal ops
body: Crew sleep period 20:30–06:00 GMT shall not be interrupted by ground except for genuine safety emergencies. Pages outside this window queue to morning brief.
